topics.label: Course overview and introduction to cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture topics, outlines learning outcomes, and establishes the framework of cancer hallmarks driving the loss of cellular growth control.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades, such as Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinase pathways, enable sustained proliferation and independence from normal growth controls.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how oncogenic events arrest cells in immature, proliferative states rather than completing lineage differentiation, illustrating this across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 family regulation
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the molecular mechanisms by which cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through disruptions in p53 signaling and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence bypass, and cellular stress barriers
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss how telomere shortening enforces senescence as a protective barrier, how cancer cells bypass this via telomerase reactivation, and how p53 integrates stress signals before concluding the review of cell-autonomous growth hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They explore how tumor cells alter their metabolic state through aerobic glycolysis, maintain tissue-of-origin metabolic wiring, and acquire Krebs cycle mutations that produce oncogenic metabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: It details how expanding tumors overcome oxygen diffusion limits by activating the angiogenic switch to stimulate new blood vessel growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They address the complex stages of metastatic dissemination, methods for tracking circulating tumor cells, environmental constraints governing secondary colonization, and the clonal genomic features of metastatic lesions.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It synthesises how varied mutational trajectories converge on common hallmark capabilities and concludes the lecture.
